brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Seamline, the open-source command-line tool in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: precise, trustworthy, developer-native; it must work in a terminal-heavy README, as a GitHub avatar and on a small docs site. No database cylinders, no elephants, no generic terminal prompt. Web and GitHub only.

claim.notes: No concept cleared the quality gate after two rounds (live-through 6.38, stepped-s 5.92, offset-seam dropped at sketch review), so nothing was finalized, exported, installed or gallery-built.

concepts.title: Live Through
readsAs: three stacked bars (list or equals sign)
a toggle or stacked-layers UI glyph
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a division sign or plus-minus (UI icon, struck); s2 a pause, Ø or slashed disc (struck); s3 a dollar sign (cliché, struck); s4 two bars with a wave between them, close to a data stream between two tables. Pick s4 because it is the only one that carries the idea (a live line passing between shifting schemas) and is not a stock glyph. Fixes: the slab offset is barely visible at 32 px, so make the shove bigger, fewer in number and more asymmetric. Thicken the wave and give it a clear S-curve so it does not read as a tilde or an equals sign. Keep the two colours but raise the contrast of the orange against the green. Check that it does not collapse to a strikethrough at 16 px. If it does, this is a weak pick.

concepts.title: Offset Seam
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a stair step or L-block; s2 a square with a swirl or Z cut, near a pinwheel or Liquibase-like block; s3 the letter S or 5 in a pixel font; s4 a rounded app tile with a squiggle slit. All four are a stock block plus a notch, and a stranger does not get a migration or a seam from any of them. s3 is a letter, so it is struck. s2 and s4 are the best, but I would not bet 7 or higher on distinctiveness and memorability. Try a different move: drop the block-with-cut. Build the mark from two shapes that really are offset, such as two bars or two L-forms that share one continuous edge, so the shared seam is the figure and not a cut in a tile.

concepts.title: Stepped S
readsAs: blue disc with a slot cut (app-icon badge)
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 squared S or 5, Greek-key; s2 two hooks forming an S, split by a hairline; s3 S tile, app-icon-like and heavy; s4 S in a tile, close to s1. Pick s2: lowest stock similarity (40%), holds as S at 16px, the out-of-register offset carries the seam idea and is not a UI icon. Fix: confirm it does not read as digit 5 at 16px, make the hairline survive at 16px (widen), and push the offset so it is the memorable hook.
